microsoft.legal_scope: Microsoft Corporation global group; exact UK subsidiary mapping and current group structure not established.
microsoft.change: October 2026 CMA proposed SMS designation spans five business-software areas. This is a proposal, not an enacted remedy. Historical March 2025 CMA reasoning separately describes Azure compute supporting model training and downstream access; it does not establish 2026 OpenAI control.
microsoft.ecosystem: March 2025 CMA summary distinguishes material influence from de facto control over OpenAI. Azure infrastructure, own models and Copilot-integrated software are different roles; an alliance is not ownership or evidence of a named customer delivery.
microsoft.implication: Interpretation: application licensing, cloud portability and model-access dependencies should be assessed separately. No quantified customer switching cost or sales demand has been established.
microsoft.critical_gap: Current partnership terms and named UK operating entities require fresh permitted primary disclosures.

aws.legal_scope: Amazon Web Services is a business/brand reference. AMAZON WEB SERVICES EMEA SARL remains a distinct unresolved foreign legal identity; no UK subsidiary substitution.
aws.change: September 2024 HMT reported a planned five-year £8bn AWS UK investment. The £14bn GDP estimate has its own 2024–2028 scope. Neither statement measures realised investment or current UK revenue.
aws.ecosystem: Government-announced infrastructure investment and a CMA cloud investigation describe investment and market scrutiny, not a Lloyds/easyJet delivery contract. January 2025 provisional CMA recommendations are retained as historical and superseded.
aws.implication: Interpretation: capacity, portability and concentration are separate research dimensions. Delivery partners, operating regions, UK workforce and completed capacity remain unverified.
aws.critical_gap: Current permitted UK operating disclosure, authoritative EMEA legal linkage and evidence of investment execution.

darktrace.legal_scope: DARKTRACE LIMITED, 13264637, active register entry. Group/brand and parent ownership links are proposals only; not inferred from the shared name.
darktrace.change: DSIT 2025 analysis places Darktrace among dedicated UK-headquartered firms offering cyber-security-for-AI products/services. This is a dated sector classification, not product-by-product efficacy or current UK-headcount evidence.
darktrace.ecosystem: DSIT identifies a sector cohort of approximately 31 dedicated firms; that number is not Darktrace revenue, customer count or employees. No bank/airline adoption or managed-service partnership follows from the list.
darktrace.implication: Interpretation: AI security assurance is relevant to customer-facing digital services. Investigate the actual threat model and deployment before inferring an unmet need.
darktrace.critical_gap: Permitted current product/operating disclosure and evidenced group ownership; no independently verified performance claim.

computacenter.legal_scope: COMPUTACENTER (UK) LIMITED, 01584718, active. Exact name matches both register and the GCA supplier heading; current parent/group relationships remain unknown.
computacenter.change: GCA supplier page lists Cloud Compute 2, Professional Services and Software. An undated procurement catalogue is evidence of a listing only; supplier eligibility, award, order and delivered outcome must remain separate.
computacenter.ecosystem: The catalogue spans infrastructure, professional services and software procurement routes. It does not identify current customers, subcontractors, manufacturer alliances, contract values or delivery responsibility.
computacenter.implication: Interpretation: a cross-category route suggests questions about integration and managed operations. The current official issuer-results URL has been discovered but its body is withheld pending reuse-policy clearance.
computacenter.critical_gap: Rights-cleared current service/operating structure and comparable UK turnover; catalogue listing alone is not a substantive current enterprise baseline.

td-synnex.legal_scope: TD SYNNEX UK LIMITED, 01691472, active. Historical Tech Data global context is not proof of the current UK legal entity’s parent or operating scope.
td-synnex.change: EC July 2021 merger text describes Tech Data as a global technology wholesaler supplying resellers. Preserve this as dated pre-integration role evidence; do not relabel it as current UK turnover or current divisional structure.
td-synnex.ecosystem: Wholesale distribution to resellers differs from end-customer systems integration. No current vendor authorisation, resale contract or downstream bank/airline delivery has been established.
td-synnex.implication: Interpretation: channel dependency, vendor concentration and lifecycle support are research questions. Brand succession and current UK offers require separate evidence.
td-synnex.critical_gap: Current group/brand lineage and rights-cleared UK business model; historical EC context is insufficient for a complete current channel baseline.

oxford-ionics.legal_scope: OXFORD IONICS LIMITED, 11795789, active; selected register SIC includes computer/peripheral manufacture, electrical equipment and engineering. SIC is a filed category, not a measured capability.
oxford-ionics.change: September 2025 final-order conditions require UK hosting for independent assessment and maintenance of science, engineering, infrastructure and related manufacturing functions. Conditions are not proof of compliance or acquisition completion.
oxford-ionics.ecosystem: The order specifically concerns trapped-ion quantum hardware and UK validation capacity. It does not establish production readiness, commercial advantage, adoption by Lloyds/easyJet or a procurement programme.
oxford-ionics.implication: Interpretation: evidence of evaluation access, maturity and applicable workloads is needed before commercialisation. A legal safeguard is not a supplier performance benchmark.
oxford-ionics.critical_gap: Current ownership/completion status, evidence of fulfilled conditions, technology readiness and actual workloads.

new_sources.excerpt:
Microsoft is a global technology company. The cloud compute services that Microsoft supplies through Azure are used for training foundation models (FMs) and also as a platform for downstream customers to access FMs.
In particular the CMA does not consider there has been a change of control by Microsoft from material influence to de facto control over OpenAI.
A finding that the Partnership does not give rise to a relevant merger situation does not constitute a finding that no competition concerns arise from its operation.

AWS-PLAN.text: The Chancellor Rachel Reeves has today [11 September] confirmed an £8 billion investment from Amazon Web Services which is estimated to support thousands of jobs across the UK. The Chancellor secured the planned five-year investment last week at a meeting with Amazon Web Services. AWS estimates that these investments in the UK will contribute £14 billion to the UK’s total Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from 2024 to 2028.

MS-SOFTWARE.text:
CMA proposes to designate Microsoft with strategic market status in its business software ecosystem.
Microsoft’s strength in business software comes from the barriers customers face when switching, limiting their choice and weakening the constraints of other software developers
Microsoft has a strong position across each of the 5 areas of digital activity that the CMA investigated (personal computer operating systems, productivity software suites, security software, server operating systems and relational database management systems)
Assessing whether customers can freely choose the best AI tools and functionalities for their needs, and whether alternative AI providers have a level playing field to compete with Microsoft’s Copilot

MS-OPENAI-2025.locator: Summary paragraphs 2,3,15; selected non-contiguous sentences; historical decision
MS-OPENAI-2025.text:
Microsoft is a global technology company. The cloud compute services that Microsoft supplies through Azure are used for training foundation models (FMs) and also as a platform for downstream customers to access FMs.
In particular the CMA does not consider there has been a change of control by Microsoft from material influence to de facto control over OpenAI.
A finding that the Partnership does not give rise to a relevant merger situation does not constitute a finding that no competition concerns arise from its operation.
